ex150:
static let dumbbellCurlContent = ExerciseContent(
        annotations: [
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "shoulder", label: "Shoulders down",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.303, y: 0.12),
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "upper_arm_R"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "elbow", label: "Elbows at sides",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.682, y: 0.16),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "forearm_L"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "grip", label: "Wrists straight",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.318, y: 0.60),
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "hand_R"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "torso", label: "No body swing",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.712, y: 0.76),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "thigh_L"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "range", label: "Straight arms",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.712, y: 0.60),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "hand_L")
        ],
        cues: [
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "shoulder",
                title: "Shoulder Position",
                intro: "The shoulders stay down and back while the arms curl.",
                why: "Shrugging brings the upper traps into the lift, and rolling the shoulders forward carries the upper arms off their fixed place, so the curl stops being an elbow-only movement.",
                mistake: "Shoulders shrugging up and rolling forward as the dumbbells reach the top.",
                correct: "Set the shoulders down and back before the first rep and keep them level and still to the top of every curl."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "elbow",
                title: "Elbow Position",
                intro: "The elbows stay by your sides; only the forearms move.",
                why: "With the upper arms still, bending the elbows is the only motion, so the elbow flexors lift the dumbbells. Letting the elbows drift forward brings the front deltoids in and turns the top of the curl into a front raise.",
                mistake: "Elbows drifting forward and up as the dumbbells rise.",
                correct: "Keep the elbows close to the ribs and finish each curl with the dumbbells in front of the chest, palms facing the shoulders, the elbows still at your sides."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "grip",
                title: "Grip and Wrists",
                intro: "Palms forward from the start and turned up all the way, wrists straight.",
                why: "In trained lifters, curls with the palms turned up have worked the biceps harder than palm-in or palm-down curls. Curling the wrists in moves the weight with the wrists instead of the elbows, and a bent wrist grips far more weakly.",
                mistake: "Wrists curling in toward the forearms as the dumbbells reach the top.",
                correct: "Hold the handles palms-forward with the arms hanging, keep the palms turned up as they rise, and keep the knuckles in line with the forearms from bottom to top."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "torso",
                title: "Body Swing",
                intro: "The legs and back stay out of it.",
                why: "Leaning back or pushing the hips forward borrows momentum from the hips and lower back to get the dumbbells moving, so the elbow flexors skip the heaviest part of the rep, with the forearms near level.",
                mistake: "Leaning back and pushing the hips forward to swing the dumbbells up.",
                correct: "Stand tall and braced, curl in about a second, pause briefly at the top and take about two seconds to lower, so each rep starts from a still body."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "range",
                title: "Range of Motion",
                intro: "Each rep starts from straight arms.",
                why: "The first part of the curl is the lightest, so it is easy to cut short. Lowering until the arms are straight takes the elbow flexors through their whole range, and in new lifters, full-range curl training has built more strength than mid-range partial reps.",
                mistake: "Short reps that turn round with the elbows still bent, the dumbbells never getting back to the thighs.",
                correct: "Lower under control until the arms hang straight by your sides, then curl again without bouncing."
            )
        ],
        activation: [
            MuscleActivation(name: "Biceps Brachii", rank: .primary, fraction: 0.86),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Brachialis", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.66),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Brachioradialis", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.44),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Forearms", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.30)
        ],
        stabilisers: ["anterior deltoid", "upper trapezius", "core"],
        setup: [
            "Hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.",
            "Stand tall, feet hip-width, arms straight by your sides.",
            "Draw your shoulders down and back, elbows by your ribs.",
            "Curl both dumbbells together, palms turned up."
        ],
        comparison: FormComparisonCopy(
            correctBadge: "CORRECT FORM",
            mistakeBadge: "ELBOWS DRIFTING FORWARD",
            correctCue: "Elbows fixed at your sides",
            mistakeCue: "Elbows swing forward and up",
            correctNote: "With the elbows at the sides, the elbow flexors lift the dumbbells from straight arms to the top.",
            mistakeNote: "When the elbows travel forward, the front deltoids join in and the top of the curl turns into a front raise."
        ),
        glows: [
            .init(DS.activation.opacity(0.55), rx: 0.06, ry: 0.07, cx: 0.69, cy: 0.30),
            .init(DS.activation.opacity(0.55), rx: 0.06, ry: 0.07, cx: 0.38, cy: 0.31),
            .init(DS.activationSoft.opacity(0.28), rx: 0.04, ry: 0.05, cx: 0.71, cy: 0.35)
        ]
    )

    static let inclineDumbbellCurlContent = ExerciseContent(
        annotations: [
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "back", label: "Back on the pad",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.318, y: 0.24),
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "spine"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "arms", label: "Elbows point to the floor",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.536, y: 0.80),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "forearm_L"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "shoulder", label: "Shoulders back",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.303, y: 0.16),
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "upper_arm_R"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "grip", label: "Flat wrists",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.259, y: 0.45),
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "hand_R"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "range", label: "Almost straight",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.682, y: 0.66),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "forearm_L")
        ],
        cues: [
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "back",
                title: "Bench and Back",
                intro: "An incline bench, the back flat on the pad.",
                why: "Leaning back with the arms hanging extends the shoulders, which stretches the biceps' long head, the head that starts above the shoulder joint. That is what sets the incline curl apart; a bench set upright, or sitting up off it, leaves the arms in line with the body as in an ordinary seated curl.",
                mistake: "The bench set too upright, or sitting up off it, so the arms hang in line with the body instead of behind it.",
                correct: "Set the back pad to about 65°, sit back with the hips at the back of the seat, and keep the back on the pad from the first rep to the last."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "arms",
                title: "Upper Arm Position",
                intro: "The upper arms hang straight down and stay there.",
                why: "Hanging from a reclined trunk, the upper arms sit behind the body, where the long head is stretched. Letting the elbows swing forward as the dumbbells rise gives that position up and brings the front deltoids into the lift.",
                mistake: "Elbows swinging forward as the dumbbells rise, the upper arms ending in front of the body.",
                correct: "Let the arms hang straight down from the shoulders, elbows pointing at the floor, and move only the forearms."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "shoulder",
                title: "Shoulder Position",
                intro: "The shoulders stay back against the pad.",
                why: "Rolling the shoulders forward off the pad carries the upper arms forward with them, so they stop hanging behind the body and the long head loses its stretch.",
                mistake: "Shoulders rolling forward off the pad as the dumbbells reach the top.",
                correct: "Keep the shoulder blades against the pad, chest up, and let only the forearms move."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "grip",
                title: "Grip and Wrists",
                intro: "Palms forward at the bottom and turned up all the way, wrists straight.",
                why: "In trained lifters, curls with the palms turned up have worked the biceps harder than palm-in or palm-down curls. Curling the wrists in moves the weight with the wrists instead of the elbows, and a bent wrist grips far more weakly.",
                mistake: "Wrists curling in toward the forearms as the dumbbells reach the top.",
                correct: "Hold the handles palms-forward with the arms hanging, keep the palms turned up as they rise, and keep the knuckles in line with the forearms."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "range",
                title: "Range of Motion",
                intro: "Each rep starts with the arms almost straight.",
                why: "The bottom of the incline curl is where the long head is longest and the dumbbells pull least on the elbows, so it is easy to cut short. Lowering until the arms are almost straight works the elbow flexors through nearly their whole range, and in new lifters, full-range curl training has built more strength than mid-range partial reps.",
                mistake: "Turning each rep round halfway down, the elbows still well bent.",
                correct: "Lower under control until the arms are almost straight below the shoulders, then curl again without bouncing."
            )
        ],
        activation: [
            MuscleActivation(name: "Biceps Brachii", rank: .primary, fraction: 0.86),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Brachialis", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.66),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Brachioradialis", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.44),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Forearms", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.30)
        ],
        stabilisers: ["anterior deltoid"],
        setup: [
            "Set the back pad of an incline bench to about 65°.",
            "Sit back, back and shoulders on the pad, feet flat.",
            "Hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.",
            "Let your arms hang straight down, behind your body."
        ],
        comparison: FormComparisonCopy(
            correctBadge: "CORRECT FORM",
            mistakeBadge: "ELBOWS SWINGING FORWARD",
            correctCue: "Arms hang behind the body",
            mistakeCue: "Elbows swing forward",
            correctNote: "With the upper arms hanging straight down from a reclined trunk, the biceps curl the dumbbells from their stretched position behind the body.",
            mistakeNote: "When the elbows swing forward, the arms leave the stretched position behind the body and the front deltoids help lift."
        ),
        glows: [
            .init(DS.activation.opacity(0.55), rx: 0.05, ry: 0.07, cx: 0.76, cy: 0.35),
            .init(DS.activationSoft.opacity(0.28), rx: 0.04, ry: 0.05, cx: 0.78, cy: 0.41)
        ]
    )

    static let preacherCurlContent = ExerciseContent(
        annotations: [
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "pad", label: "Arms on pads",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.274, y: 0.75),
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "forearm_R"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "range", label: "Almost straight",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.318, y: 0.16),
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "hand_R"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "grip", label: "Wrists straight",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.318, y: 0.59),
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "hand_R"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "torso", label: "No rocking back",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.682, y: 0.68),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "thigh_L"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "seat", label: "Seat set",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.785, y: 0.80),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "foot_L")
        ],
        cues: [
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "pad",
                title: "Arms on the Pads",
                intro: "The backs of the upper arms stay on the pads.",
                why: "The pads hold the upper arms at about 45° in front of the body, so bending the elbows is the only motion and the shoulders cannot help lift.",
                mistake: "Elbows and upper arms lifting off the pads as the bar comes up.",
                correct: "Rest the backs of the arms on the pads with the armpits just over their top edges, and keep the elbows down on them for the whole set."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "range",
                title: "Range of Motion",
                intro: "The bottom half is where a preacher curl works hardest.",
                why: "With the upper arms on a slope, the bar pulls hardest on the elbows from almost straight to level forearms and hardly at all once they are near upright; in new lifters on preacher curls, training the lower range has built more strength, and at least as much muscle, as training the upper range.",
                mistake: "Stopping halfway down, so the arms never get near straight.",
                correct: "Lower under control until the arms are almost straight, without letting the elbows snap straight, then curl again."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "grip",
                title: "EZ Bar Grip",
                intro: "Hands on the angled grips, wrists straight.",
                why: "The angled grips turn the palms partly in from fully up. Next to a straight bar the difference in biceps activity has been small, so the choice of bar is largely a matter of comfort. Curling the wrists in moves the bar with the wrists instead of the elbows, and a bent wrist grips far more weakly.",
                mistake: "Curling the wrists in toward the forearms at the top of each rep.",
                correct: "Take the inner angled grips underhand, about shoulder-width apart, thumbs around the bar, and keep the knuckles in line with the forearms from bottom to top."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "torso",
                title: "Torso Position",
                intro: "Sit tall; the torso stays still.",
                why: "Rocking back uses the body's weight to start the lift and pulls the arms off the pads, so the elbow flexors skip the hardest part of the rep at the bottom.",
                mistake: "Leaning back from the hips to heave the bar up, the arms coming off the pads.",
                correct: "Sit tall with the feet flat, brace the core and keep the torso upright and still; only the forearms move."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "seat",
                title: "Seat Height",
                intro: "Set the seat before the first rep.",
                why: "At the right height the backs of the arms lie on the pads with the shoulders relaxed; too low, the shoulders hunch up to hook the arms over them.",
                mistake: "The seat set too low, the shoulders riding up toward the ears to reach over the pads.",
                correct: "Raise or lower the seat until the armpits sit just over the tops of the pads with the shoulders down, then plant both feet flat."
            )
        ],
        activation: [
            MuscleActivation(name: "Biceps Brachii", rank: .primary, fraction: 0.84),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Brachialis", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.66),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Brachioradialis", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.38),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Forearms", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.30)
        ],
        stabilisers: ["anterior deltoid", "core"],
        setup: [
            "Set the seat so your armpits sit just over the arm pads.",
            "Take an EZ bar underhand on its angled grips, about shoulder-width.",
            "Rest the backs of your upper arms on the pads, arms almost straight.",
            "Sit tall with both feet flat."
        ],
        comparison: FormComparisonCopy(
            correctBadge: "CORRECT FORM",
            mistakeBadge: "STOPPING SHORT AT THE BOTTOM",
            correctCue: "Lower to almost straight",
            mistakeCue: "Reps stop halfway down",
            correctNote: "Lowering until the arms are almost straight trains the bottom half, where the preacher curl loads the biceps most.",
            mistakeNote: "Stopping halfway keeps every rep in the top half, where the bar moves in over the elbows and the load on the biceps falls away."
        ),
        glows: [
            .init(DS.activation.opacity(0.55), rx: 0.05, ry: 0.05, cx: 0.79, cy: 0.32),
            .init(DS.activation.opacity(0.55), rx: 0.05, ry: 0.05, cx: 0.52, cy: 0.34),
            .init(DS.activationSoft.opacity(0.28), rx: 0.04, ry: 0.04, cx: 0.76, cy: 0.36)
        ]
    )

    static let cableCurlContent = ExerciseContent(
        annotations: [
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "elbow", label: "Arms at sides",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.712, y: 0.32),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "forearm_L"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "top", label: "Curl all the way up",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.376, y: 0.16),
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "hand_L"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "range", label: "Almost straight",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.682, y: 0.52),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "forearm_L"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "grip", label: "Flat wrists",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.259, y: 0.24),
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "hand_L"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "torso", label: "No swinging",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.741, y: 0.60),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "pelvis")
        ],
        cues: [
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "elbow",
                title: "Elbow Position",
                intro: "The elbows stay by your sides; only the forearms move.",
                why: "With the upper arms still, bending the elbows is the only motion, so the elbow flexors move the handles. At the bottom the cables pull the arms toward the pulleys; letting the elbows drift forward brings the front deltoids in and turns the top of the curl into a front raise.",
                mistake: "Elbows drifting forward and up as the handles rise.",
                correct: "Keep the elbows close to the ribs from the bottom to the top and curl without swinging them forward."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "top",
                title: "Top of the Curl",
                intro: "Each rep finishes with the handles in front of the chest.",
                why: "With the pulleys low and about a metre in front, the cables pull hardest from the middle of the curl all the way to the top. Stopping halfway gives up the part of the rep the cables load most.",
                mistake: "Stopping each rep halfway up, the forearms only just past level.",
                correct: "Curl until the handles are in front of the chest, pause briefly, then lower under control."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "range",
                title: "Range of Motion",
                intro: "Each rep starts with the arms almost straight.",
                why: "At the bottom the cables run forward from the hands, above the line of the forearms, so they pull the hands forward instead of resisting the first part of the curl, which is light and easy to cut short. Lowering until the arms are almost straight still takes the elbows through nearly their whole range.",
                mistake: "Short reps that turn round with the elbows still bent, the handles never getting back to the thighs.",
                correct: "Lower under control until the arms are almost straight by your sides, the stacks still just off their rests, then curl again."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "grip",
                title: "Grip and Wrists",
                intro: "An underhand grip, wrists straight.",
                why: "In trained lifters, curls with the palms turned up have worked the biceps harder than palm-in or palm-down curls. Curling the wrists in moves the weight with the wrists instead of the elbows, and a bent wrist grips far more weakly.",
                mistake: "Wrists curling in toward the forearms as the handles reach the top.",
                correct: "Hold the handles palms-forward with the arms hanging, keep the palms turned up as they rise, and keep the knuckles in line with the forearms."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "torso",
                title: "Body Position",
                intro: "A slight lean back, held still.",
                why: "The cables pull the hands forward and down, and a small lean back keeps you balanced against them. Rocking further back or pushing the hips forward to heave the handles up borrows momentum from the hips and lower back, so the elbow flexors skip part of the work.",
                mistake: "Rocking back and pushing the hips forward to swing the handles up.",
                correct: "Stand tall with the feet hip-width, lean back just enough to stay balanced against the cables and hold that position from the first rep to the last."
            )
        ],
        activation: [
            MuscleActivation(name: "Biceps Brachii", rank: .primary, fraction: 0.84),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Brachialis", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.66),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Brachioradialis", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.44),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Forearms", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.30)
        ],
        stabilisers: ["anterior deltoid", "pectoralis major", "core"],
        setup: [
            "Attach a D-handle to the low pulley of each of two columns.",
            "Take a handle in each hand, palms facing forward.",
            "Step back about a metre until both stacks lift.",
            "Stand tall, feet hip-width, arms almost straight, leaning back slightly."
        ],
        comparison: FormComparisonCopy(
            correctBadge: "CORRECT FORM",
            mistakeBadge: "STOPPING SHORT AT THE TOP",
            correctCue: "Handles to the chest",
            mistakeCue: "Reps stop halfway up",
            correctNote: "Curling the handles up to the chest trains the top of the curl, where the low cables in front still pull hard.",
            mistakeNote: "Stopping halfway gives up the top of the curl, the part the cables load most, and turns each rep into a half rep."
        ),
        glows: [
            .init(DS.activation.opacity(0.55), rx: 0.05, ry: 0.07, cx: 0.62, cy: 0.29),
            .init(DS.activationSoft.opacity(0.28), rx: 0.04, ry: 0.05, cx: 0.60, cy: 0.35)
        ]
    )

    static let bayesianCableCurlContent = ExerciseContent(
        annotations: [
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "elbow", label: "Upper arm still",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.682, y: 0.16),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "upper_arm_L"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "range", label: "Almost straight",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.682, y: 0.30),
                          labelSide: .trailing,
                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "forearm_L"),
            CueAnnotation(cueID: "grip", label: "Flat wrist",
                          labelPoint: CGPoint(x: 0.244, y: 0.30),

        ],
        cues: [
            TechniqueCue(
